subject: E-Commerce
title: Progress Bars at Checkout
description: One-minute skill: Progress Bars at Checkout.

hook.text: Adding a progress bar to checkout ('Step 2 of 3') increases conversion by 28%. People finish what they start.

buildup.text: The Zeigarnik effect says incomplete tasks nag at our minds. A progress bar exploits this drive to finish.

discovery.text: Starting the bar at 20% complete tricks the brain into thinking it's already invested. Abandoning feels wasteful.

twist.text: LinkedIn used a progress bar for profiles: 'Your profile is 65% complete.' It drove millions to add more info.

climax.text: Progress bars turn checkout from a chore into a mission. Completion becomes the goal, not just buying.

punchline.text: Step 2 of 3, 28% more conversions. People can't resist finishing what they.

quiz.question: What psychological effect makes progress bars work?
options: The Zeigarnik effect—people feel compelled to finish incomplete tasks
